own_solution.law: Snell's law plus Fresnel p-polarisation reflection coefficient: r_p = (n cos(thi) - cos(tht))/(n cos(thi) + cos(tht)); P_in = P (1 - r_p^2) for a lossless interface
assumptions: lossless, non-absorbing glass; energy conservation T = 1 - R
power at laser equals power at the surface (no losses in air)

notes: sin(tht) = sin75/1.5 = 0.64395, cos(tht) = 0.76507, cos75 = 0.25882; r_p = (0.38823-0.76507)/(0.38823+0.76507) = -0.32675; R = 0.10677, T = 0.89323. P_in = 5 x 0.89323 = 4.466 mW; with amplifier on the beam, 8.4 x 0.89323 = 7.503 mW. Beam area cancels (intensity times area is power; Fresnel coefficients are independent of area). Area variants T6A28/T8526 both state 5.5 mm^2. The amplifier sentences TBC5B, T38E1, TAC23, T6921 all state 3.4 mW; T01A0 and TA9F7 state 'a small amount' with no number, so if they are meant as minimal-pair variants of the 3.4 mW sentences they differ in the value, not only in attachment. Their attachments (earlier run, second laser) make them D anyway.
